summary.text: A 3-day-old full-term infant with a history of severe perinatal asphyxia was transferred for emesis, lethargy and abdominal distension for 4 hours, then presented with bilious vomiting and developed bloody stools, fever and weakened bowel sounds.

Stage IIIA NEC was confirmed using clinical signs, radiography and ultrasonography; X-ray showed portal venous gas, TAT markedly increased and sTM mildly increased, and mNGS of ascites grew Clostridium butyricum with a negative blood culture. PIC was elevated together with TAT.

The infant did not undergo surgery, received antibiotics for 12 days (cefmetazole and ampicillin listed after mNGS) and enoxaparin anticoagulant therapy for 14 days, was discharged without complications and had a length of stay of 20 days. The documentation of sex conflicts between Table 1 (girl) and the text (he).

summary.text: An 8-day-old preterm girl (36 weeks, 2,125 g, Apgar 9–10) was hospitalized with fever, abdominal distension and hematochezia after achieving full enteral feeding at 7 days of age.

Ileocolic resection and ileostomy were performed; stage IIIB NEC was diagnosed with ileal perforation, pneumoperitoneum on X-ray and increased TAT and sTM. Ascitic mNGS grew fecal coliform, Enterococcus faecalis and Escherichia coli, blood culture was negative and CSF showed a white blood cell count of 27 × 10⁶/L with negative nucleic acid testing.

Treatment included meropenem and vancomycin after mNGS, mechanical ventilation for 5 days, dopamine for 2 days and enoxaparin as an anticoagulant for 23 days; trophic feeding began on the fifth day after the operation and oral feeding was established after 14 days. The patient was discharged tolerating feeding with normal coagulation tests after a 26-day stay.

summary.text: A 3-day-old full-term boy (39 4/7 weeks, 4,000 g) with tracheal intubation was transferred for emesis and abdominal distension for 3 days after vomiting began 6 hours after birth; examination showed skin mottling, high abdominal distension, weak bowel sounds and a capillary refill time of 4 to 5 seconds.

Laboratory examination showed decreased white blood cells, slightly increased CRP, significantly increased TAT and mildly increased sTM indicating hypercoagulability; blood culture grew Enterococcus faecium and CSF was normal. After an operation with ascending colon perforation, meconium peritonitis was diagnosed postoperatively.

Enoxaparin anticoagulation was given for 15 days, with meropenem and vancomycin after mNGS, mechanical ventilation for 6 days, HHFNC for 2 days, dopamine and epinephrine; enteral feeding was initiated 6 days after surgery and the hospital stay was 23 days.

summary.text: A newborn boy aged 24 minutes (32 4/7 weeks, 1,840 g, Apgar 9–10) was admitted because of premature birth and on the fourth day after birth presented with vomiting, abdominal distension, tachypnea and groaning; examination showed abdominal enlargement, high abdominal distension and absent bowel sounds.

Operation showed an 8 cm gastric wall muscular layer defect and a congenital gastric wall defect was diagnosed postoperatively; X-ray showed pneumoperitoneum, TAT increased on the first day after surgery suggesting hypercoagulability, and sTM varied minimally.

Enoxaparin was given as an anticoagulant for 16 days, with penicillin and meropenem after mNGS, HHFNC, IMV and nCPAP, and dopamine, dobutamine and norepinephrine; the mean time to full enteral feeding was 11 days and the hospital stay was 30 days, with discharge tolerating feeding and normal coagulation tests.

article_limitations: Table 1 gives the sex of Case 1 as girl while the case text uses "he"; both are retained as source_conflict, review-only facts.
Case 3 CRP is described as slightly increased in the case text but as markedly elevated in all four cases in the discussion; both are retained as review-only.
Biomarker values for TAT, PIC, sTM, t-PAIC, platelets, D-dimer, PT and fibrinogen are given only as figure points; no values were transcribed from the plots into facts.
The four control patients (anal atresia, post-NEC stenosis, allergic proctocolitis) are mentioned in aggregate and are not roster patients.
The discussion states LMWH was used in the unit and monitored by anti-Xa; this is unit practice and is not attributed to individual patients.
Operation type is not named for cases 3 and 4; the operation is established by "postoperatively" and the operative-findings row.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; both figure images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Narrative paragraphs b00003 to b00006 carry no case numbers; each maps to one Table 1 column through a diagnosis printed only in that column (NEC IIIA, NEC IIIB, meconium peritonitis, gastric wall defect), consistent ages, and case-named discussion sentences (b00028 case 1 asphyxia and NEC IIIA; b00030 case 3 stay of 23 days and case 4 full enteral feeding at 11 days).

Fig. 1 course bars for Case 3 and Case 4 are drawn in yellow and green, the reverse of the legend (case 3 green, case 4 yellow); colour-based series ownership for cases 3 and 4 in Fig. 1 is uncertain and no plot values are used as facts.
The discussion statement that CRP was markedly elevated in all four cases is kept review-only for every patient because the case 3 text contradicts it.
